subject: Clarification: streaming buffers vs final artifacts — retention and erasure evidence
messages:
From: Alice White <alice.white@brightbank.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: what gets persisted by default (streams vs final outputs)?

Sergio —

Thanks for taking this. BrightBank's audit team is validating vendor default retention and needs a short Q&A for our control docs. We have three specific clarifications: 

1) For the hosted API, by default which items are persisted beyond the live session? Specifically: full request payloads (prompts), partial/streamed tokens (intermediate buffers), final model outputs, and any KV/streaming caches.

2) If an external customer requests erasure for a particular session, what evidence can you provide to show deletion (audit trail, object delete logs, signed attestation)?

3) Are there hosted vs dedicated differences we should call out? If retention windows are configurable, what are the defaults and minimums we can promise in an order form?

We're collecting short answers for the SOC3 readiness pack — a couple bullets per item would be ideal. If you have an internal playbook or a one-page we can reference that would be great.

(If it's easier, feel free to loop in your compliance lead.)

Appreciate it,

--
Alice White
Senior InfoSec Manager — BrightBank
security@brightbank.com

Attachments: none
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice White <alice.white@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: what gets persisted by default (streams vs final outputs)?

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I'll follow up with attachments and Kimberly for the formal language. Short summary first, then a couple of implementation notes: 

Summary (hosted API, default behavior):
- Requests/prompts: stored by default for troubleshooting and quality monitoring. Default hosted retention window: 60 days. Customers can request shorter windows for enterprise contracts.
- Streamed/intermediate tokens: not persisted to long-term storage by default. Streams are buffered in-memory during the session and discarded immediately after the response is finalized unless a customer enables session logs.
- Final model outputs: persisted for the same default window as requests (60 days) to enable replay and debugging.
- KV cache / runtime caches: ephemeral; not written to persistent storage except where customer explicitly enables a persistent embedding/indexing feature.

Erasure evidence we can provide:
- Deletion audit trail showing the deletion job id and timestamp.
- Object lifecycle logs (S3 Delete Marker / audit entries) tied to the record(s).
- A signed attestation summarizing the deletion event (PDF) for procurement/audit teams.

Hosted vs Dedicated/Private:
- Dedicated: retention windows can be set by contract (30/60/90/180 day options). We can enable auto-purge and provide on-demand bulk deletes with audit proof.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): customer controls retention/purge; Redwood provides the runbook and tools but the customer operates deletion unless we manage the environment under a support agreement.

Next steps: I'll attach a short one-pager (RBW-data-retention-summary.pdf) and our erasure playbook excerpt; Kimberly will add the formal compliance wording you can paste into your vendor control template. Want me to include a sample audit-delete log line as well?

Best,
Sergio

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alice White <alice.white@brightbank.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: what gets persisted by default (streams vs final outputs)? — compliance wording

Alice / Sergio —

Adding a compact, copy-ready paragraph you can place in BrightBank's control documents. This reflects hosted defaults and the artifacts we can provide for deletion evidence. If you need slightly different wording for procurement/legal we can iterate.

"Redwood Inference (hosted) retains request payloads (including prompts) and final model outputs by default for a maximum of 60 days for troubleshooting, quality monitoring, and abuse detection. Streaming fragments and runtime caches (including KV caches) are kept only in volatile memory during active sessions and are not written to persistent storage unless the customer explicitly enables session logging or persistent embedding/indexing features. Upon receiving a verified erasure request, Redwood executes a deletion job that removes persisted artifacts and emits an auditable deletion record (job id, timestamp, affected object ids). Redwood can provide: (a) deletion audit logs (CSV), (b) cloud object lifecycle/delete entries, and (c) a signed deletion attestation for compliance evidence."

Notes / configurable options:
- Contracting customers (Dedicated) may select alternative retention windows (30/60/90/180 days) and enable auto-purge.
- Private/on-prem deployments are subject to the customer's retention controls; Redwood can operate deletion under a managed service SLA on request.
- We offer masking & field-level redaction options for PII-sensitive prompts at ingestion time (requires enterprise plan).

Sergio — I attached the erasure playbook excerpt and a small sample audit-delete-log file you can share directly with Alice.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
